description: Metal face masks worn by some Roman cavalry were primarily associated with cavalry display equipment, especially during the imperial period. Usually made of bronze, brass, or iron and shaped into idealized human faces, they were attached to elaborate helmets and worn in ceremonial exercises such as the hippika gymnasia, where cavalrymen demonstrated riding skill, formation discipline, and mock combat before spectators. Although some may also have offered limited facial protection, their main purpose was prestigious and theatrical, emphasizing the elite status, martial identity, and visual spectacle of Roman mounted troops.
